query: Consider the following context: During the hot dip aluminum plating process, components such as sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates will come into long-term contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum and be corroded by the aluminum liquid, greatly reducing their service life. In that context, which material can be used for prepare parts for the dipping and plating equipment and protect the equipment from erosion, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Applying an alumina-based refractory ceramic coating to the dipping and plating equipment’s parts (rollers, guide plates) will protect them from erosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum compared to uncoated, conventional metallic parts.
generation.material_initial_state: Unprotected metallic components (e.g., carbon steel) currently suffer from severe corrosion when in contact with molten aluminum.
generation.intervention: Coat the surfaces of the parts with a dense, well-adhered alumina-based refractory ceramic layer.
generation.conditions: Exposure to high-temperature (>660°C) liquid aluminum during the hot dip aluminum plating process under prolonged contact and mechanical stress.
generation.structural_mediator: The inert and high-melting-point alumina layer forms a chemically stable barrier that resists dissolution and erosion by liquid aluminum.
generation.mechanism: Due to its chemical inertness and low wettability with liquid aluminum, the alumina coating minimizes interfacial reactions and physical erosion. Its high melting point also ensures that the physical integrity of the protective layer is maintained at the operating temperature.
generation.predicted_outcome: Parts coated with the alumina-based refractory ceramic will exhibit significantly reduced corrosion rates and improved service life compared to baseline uncoated metallic components.
generation.baseline: Standard uncoated metallic parts (e.g., carbon steel) that directly contact molten aluminum routinely show rapid degradation.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is expected to hold under conditions where the alumina coating maintains its adhesion and structural integrity; challenges such as thermal shock or mechanical impact could compromise performance.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty remains regarding the long-term adhesion and durability of the ceramic coating under cyclic thermal and mechanical loads, as well as potential issues with coating application uniformity over complex geometries.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identical dipping and plating equipment parts; one set coated with the alumina-based ceramic and one uncoated (control). Subject both sets to repeated immersion in high-temperature liquid aluminum over a defined number of cycles. After the test period, evaluate the extent of corrosion by weight loss measurements, surface microscopy, and mechanical integrity tests.
measurements: Weight loss per unit surface area
Surface morphology and presence of cracks or spallation via microscopy
Retention of mechanical properties (e.g., hardness, adhesion)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alumina-coated parts do not show statistically significant improvements in corrosion resistance (e.g., lower weight loss and fewer defects) compared to the uncoated parts, then the hypothesis is falsified.
